title: Label Setup Network Rule
eyebrow: One choice during the build · Label setup, the hook step

short.lead: The build plan you approved has the hook create missing labels at three moments: when you approve a design, when the issue note is given after you approve a plan, and before a refusal over labels. One of them breaks a rule the plugin already has: no hook goes to the network while the agent is carrying out a tool call (one action, such as editing a file or running a command). The docs state the rule in docs/architecture.md (line 48) and docs/4-systems/hook-engine.md (line 93), and a test in verify.py checks it. I missed it when writing the plan. The builder found it when that test failed, and changed the test to pass, which hid the clash. Nothing is merged yet.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it means.
items: Approving a design and refusing over labels both happen when your message arrives, not during a tool call. That same message check already reads issue labels from GitHub today.

The issue note is a reminder to the agent. It comes from the delegate hook, a script that runs right after a plan is approved. Approving a plan is itself a tool call, named ExitPlanMode. Label setup there would list the repo's labels, then create up to three side by side; each of those two waits is allowed 5 seconds, so up to 10 seconds in all.
You pick which way to go
Building carries on with the /house-rules:labels command (issue #277, "A /house-rules:labels command that sets up a repo's labels on demand") while you decide.

changes: What happens when a plan over three steps is approved.
Tells the agent to create the label by hand with gh label create.
If the rule stays, it tells the agent to run /house-rules:labels when a house label is missing. If the rule changes, the hook creates the missing labels itself and says so.
Either way, the advice to create labels by hand goes.
choices: Should the issue note's hook create labels, given the no-network rule?
No: keep the rule, and point the note at /house-rules:labels
Approving a design already creates the labels before planning makes any issue. The note covers repos where the design loop is off.
Yes: create them there, and change the rule and its test
Labels appear automatically even with the design loop off, but approving a plan can then wait up to 10 seconds on GitHub.
The rule keeps tool calls fast and offline. Creating labels when you approve a design covers every repo that uses the design loop, which is every repo of yours today.

wrapup.summary: One moment in the approved plan breaks the plugin's rule that no hook goes to the network during a tool call.
wrapup.changing: Only the issue note's behaviour in hook.py, and if the rule changes, its wording in two docs and its test.
wrapup.blocking: Your answer before I merge the hook step, "The hook creates missing house labels when it first needs them".
wrapup.next: I adjust the hook step to your answer, merge it, and carry on with the last two steps: the /house-rules:labels command (issue #277) and the real-repo proof with the version bump (issue #279).
